metadata.title: David Njoku - Misses another practice Thursday
metadata.description: Njoku (shoulder) was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Njoku also was deemed a 'DNP' on Wednesday, so the tight end presumably will need to practice Friday, in some capacity, in order to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots. If Njoku ends up sidelined this weekend, Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will be in line to lead the Chargers' Week 12 TE corps.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Absent Wednesday
metadata.description: Njoku (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran tight end injured his shoulder in last Sunday's loss to the Jets but was able to return to the contest, finishing with two catches for 21 yards on four targets on 41.7 percent of the offensive snaps. It's possible Wednesday was more of a maintenance day.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Logs two catches against NYJ
metadata.description: Njoku caught two of four passes for 28 yards during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Njoku briefly left Sunday's contest after injuring his shoulder at the end of a 13-yard catch in the first quarter. The veteran tight end was cleared to return, and he ended up finishing second on the Chargers in targets behind Ladd McConkey (eight), on a day that saw Justin Herbert complete 15 of 21 passes for 131 yards and two touchdowns. Njoku and the Chargers will stay home for Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

metadata.title: David Njoku catches two passes in Week 11
metadata.description: David Njoku caught two of his four targets for 21 yards in a 27-24 loss to the Jets in Week 11.
metadata.analysis: Njoku left the game briefly to get his shoulder checked out but was able to return to action. The veteran tight end is part of a three-man rotation with Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden II, which will limit his upside going forward. He will not be a recommended fantasy option heading into Week 12 vs. the Patriots.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Back in action Sunday
metadata.description: Njoku (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Jets, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Njoku briefly exited in the first quarter after hurting his shoulder on a 13-yard catch. He was initially deemed questionable to return but has since re-entered the contest. The veteran tight end is playing just his second game after returning from a stint on IR due to a fibula injury.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Exits game with shoulder injury
metadata.description: Njoku (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
metadata.analysis: Njoku appeared to injure his shoulder while being taken down on the tail end of his 13-yard catch early in the first quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Oronde Gadsden should see a bump in offensive snaps for as long as Njoku is sidelined.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Zero catches in return from six-game absence
metadata.description: Njoku played 19 offensive snaps but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during Monday's 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Njoku's snap count Monday was predictably capped, seeing as he was on injured reserve for the Chargers' six prior games while recovering from a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. Njoku could see more involvement in the Chargers' passing attack in Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Returns to action Monday
metadata.description: Njoku (fibula) officially is listed as active for Monday night's game against the Ravens, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Since being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku -- who last played in Week 2 -- logged five consecutive limited practice listings before upgrading to full participation Saturday and being deemed questionable for Monday's contest. With his return to the lineup now confirmed, Njoku will bolster a TE corps that also includes Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden. In his only full game with the team this season, Njoku caught all five of his targets for 58 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Cardinals. Now that he's back in the mix, the 2017 first-rounder has an opportunity to reclaim enough of a role in the 0-8 Chargers offense to merit fantasy lineup consideration at his position in deeper fantasy formats going forward.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Returning for Monday night game
metadata.description: The Chargers activated Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve ahead of Monday's game against the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: After completing his second week of practice upon being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku had been listed as questionable heading into Monday. The Chargers ultimately came away encouraged enough by how Njoku looked during the week of practice to activate him, giving the team a third option at tight end for Monday's game. Due to his blocking prowess, Charlie Kolar likely will lead the position group in snaps Monday, but Njoku could usurp Oronde Gadsden as the Chargers' top pass-catching tight end as he takes the field for the first time since Week 2.

metadata.title: David Njoku (fibula) activated from IR
metadata.description: The Chargers activated TE David Njoku from injured reserve.
metadata.analysis: Njoku will return for Monday's game against the Ravens. He remains off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: David Njoku Activated from IR Ahead of Monday's Game
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (leg) has been activated from Injured Reserve ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football. Njoku has been sidelined since Week 2 with a fibula injury, but it appears he will make his return against Baltimore. Across two games before getting injured, Njoku recorded six catches for 67 yards on eight targets. Upon his return, Njoku is expected to split playing time with fellow Chargers tight ends Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden. Njoku has been a productive pass-catcher at earlier points in his career, but between his long injury layoff, questionable playing time outlook, and the Chargers' offensive question marks, the veteran tight end is tough to trust in Week 10.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Questionable to face Baltimore
metadata.description: Njoku (fibula) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: Njoku continues to progress in his recovery from fibula injury that landed him on injured reserve in late September. The veteran tight end turned eight targets into six catches for 67 yards across the first two games of the regular season prior to his injury, and his return would result in a reduced offensive workload for Oronde Gadsden.

metadata.title: David Njoku Questionable for Week 10, Still on Injured Reserve
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (fibula) is questionable to return against the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night, the team announced. Njoku has been on injured reserve since Sept. 23 and still needs to be activated for Week 10. He was limited Thursday and Friday, matching his participation in all three practices last week before he was listed as doubtful and sat out against Houston. His last appearance was against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 2, when he caught one pass for nine yards and suffered the injury. Even if the Chargers activate Njoku, keep him out of Week 10 lineups in one-tight-end leagues. Oronde Gadsden II and Charlie Kolar drew three targets apiece against Houston, and Gadsden has 19 catches for 172 yards this season. Njoku ran 19 routes in the opener against Arizona, ahead of Kolar's 13 and Gadsden's seven. He caught all five of his targets for 58 yards that day and picked up three first downs. If Njoku plays Monday, look for him to reclaim that lead in routes before putting him back into lineups.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Logs another limited practice
metadata.description: Njoku (fibula), who is still on IR, was limited in practice Friday.
metadata.analysis: Njoku's 21-day practice window was opened Nov. 4, so the Chargers still have plenty of time to activate him. The veteran wideout was limited in all three practices last week and has been limited again Thursday and Friday of this week, so he may need to log a full session Saturday to get the all-clear to suit up Monday in Baltimore. Njoku could provide a boost to a struggling Chargers offense whenever he does return -- in his lone full game of the season so far (Week 1 against Arizona), he caught all five of his targets for 58 yards.

metadata.title: David Njoku (fibula) limited in practice Friday
metadata.description: David Njoku was limited in practice on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Njoku remains on track to be good to go for Monday's game against the Ravens. He remains off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: David Njoku Logs Another Limited Practice on Friday
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (fibula) remained limited during practice on Friday ahead of Week 10, according to the team's official injury report. Njoku is currently on injured reserve, and it remains unclear whether the Chargers will choose to activate him for this week's Monday Night Football contest against the Baltimore Ravens. It's worth noting that Njoku also logged two limited practices in Week 9, but did not end up getting activated prior to kickoff. Therefore, he may need to log a full practice on Saturday in order to have a realistic chance of playing this week. The 30-year-old posted a solid stat line of five catches and 58 yards during his only healthy game of the season back in Week 1. If he does play this week, he could be in the mix to handle a very large target share with wide receiver Ladd McConkey (back, did not practice) trending in the wrong direction. In such a scenario, Njoku would rank as a mid-range TE2 with low-end TE1 upside.

metadata.title: David Njoku (fibula) limited in practice Thursday
metadata.description: David Njoku was limited in practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Njoku remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Limited at practice
metadata.description: Njoku (fibula) was a limited participant at the Chargers' practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Njoku remained limited at the team's first practice of the week as he continues to work his way back from a fibula injury that has sidelined him since Week 2. The tight end was a limited participant at the team's three practices last week, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice prior to Monday night's matchup with the Ravens.

metadata.title: David Njoku Remains Limited as Prep for Week 10 Begins
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (fibula) was a limited participant in practice on Thursday, according to the team's official injury report. Njoku, who is currently on injured reserve, logged two limited sessions last week. Therefore, although Thursday's participation level is a step in the right direction, it's still far from a guarantee that he'll play in Week 10 against the Baltimore Ravens. The good news is that the Chargers play on Monday night, giving Njoku an extra day to get healthy as he continues to work his way back from a fibula injury that he suffered in Week 2. Njoku had five catches for 58 yards in his only fully healthy game this season, and he is expected to be a key part of the passing attack if activated, especially with wide receivers Ladd McConkey (back) and Tre' Harris (shoulder) uncertain for this week. Managers should stay tuned for updates on Njoku's status after the Chargers wrap up practice on Friday and Saturday.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Not activated ahead of Week 9
metadata.description: Njoku (fibula) wasn't activated from IR-designated to return ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, per the NFL's official transaction log.
metadata.analysis: Njoku returned to practice this week, but was limited all three days before being deemed doubtful for Week 9 action. The TE's next chance to play will arrive Monday Nov. 16, when the Chargers face the Ravens.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Doubtful for Sunday
metadata.description: Njoku (fibula) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Texans.
metadata.analysis: Njoku returned to practice this week but never advanced from limited participation to full. He could have a real shot next week when the Chargers face the Ravens. In the meantime, Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will get most of the TE snaps for Los Angeles.

metadata.title: David Njoku (fibula) limited in practice Thursday
metadata.description: David Njoku was limited in practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Njoku is on track to have a chance to return this weekend. He will remain off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Limited Thursday
metadata.description: Njoku (fibula) was limited in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Njoku had his 21-day practice window opener Wednesday, and he's logged back-to-back limited practice sessions to begin Week 9 work. He's been on the shelf since going down with the lower leg injury in Week 2.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Cleared to resume practicing
metadata.description: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Njoku (fibula) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
metadata.analysis: The transaction opens up a 21-day window wherein Njoku can be evaluated for a return to the 53-man roster. The veteran tight end has been out of action since sustaining the fibula injury Week 2, but if he's able to turn in a full practice at some point over the next three days, he could have a chance at being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans. Once he's back in the fold, Njoku could push Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden for snaps at tight end.

metadata.title: David Njoku's Practice Window Opens Ahead of Week 9
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (leg) has had his practice window opened as he works toward returning from injured reserve, according to Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com. Head coach Jim Harbaugh announced the development Wednesday, bringing Njoku closer to his first appearance since suffering a lower-leg injury against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 2. The 30-year-old caught six passes for 67 yards across two games before being placed on injured reserve September 23. He recorded five receptions for 58 yards in his only full outing. Oronde Gadsden II has handled an expanded role during Njoku's absence, recording 17 receptions for 155 yards and a touchdown this season, including five catches for 52 yards against the Rams last week. Njoku's eventual return could affect the distribution of tight end targets, with Charlie Kolar also part of the rotation. His availability for Sunday's matchup against the Houston Texans remains uncertain, making him a speculative stash in deeper fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Approaching return to practice
metadata.description: Coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that the Chargers will likely open the return window for Njoku (fibula) this week, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Njoku landed on IR after sustaining a fibula injury in Week 2, but the tight end's looming return to practice should provide a nice boost to a Chargers' TE corps that also includes Oronde Gadsden and Charlie Kolar. In his only full game with the team (Week 1 versus the Cardinals), Njoku recorded a 55 percent snap share en route to catching all five of his targets for 58 yards. If he can approach that level of production once he's back in the lineup, Njoku could resurface as a fantasy option as the season rolls along.

metadata.title: Chargers likely to open return window for David Njoku this week
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said on Monday that the team will likely open the return window for tight end David Njoku (leg) this week, according to Alex Insdorf. Njoku injured his fibula in the Week 2 loss to the division-rival Las Vegas Raiders and has been on Injured Reserve since, but the 30-year-old veteran could have a chance to return this weekend to face the Houston Texans if he returns to practice this week. It does not make him an attractive waiver-wire pickup going into Week 9, though, as Njoku will be battling for playing time and targets with tight ends Oronde Gadsden and Charlie Kolar when he returns, and he is not guaranteed to be back this Sunday against the Texans. Before injuring his leg and landing on IR, Njoku caught six of eight targets for 67 yards and no touchdowns. He has the most experience (nine-plus years) in the NFL among L.A.'s tight end options, but given how poorly the Chargers' offense has played this year, Njoku is not a recommended TE target as he nears his return from injury.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Lands on IR
metadata.description: The Chargers placed Njoku (fibula) on injured reserve Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Njoku will be sidelined for at least the Chargers' next four games after sustaining a fibula injury in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders. Fellow tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm) was able to avoid placement on IR but has already been ruled out for the Chargers' Week 3 contest in Buffalo, leaving Oronde Gadsden as the top option on the depth chart heading into that game.

metadata.title: David Njoku (knee) placed on IR
metadata.description: The Chargers placed TE David Njoku on injured reserve.
metadata.analysis: Njoku was carted off the field in Sunday's game against the Raiders. With Charlie Kolar (forearm) also placed on IR, Oronde Gadsden is the only healthy tight end on the Chargers right now.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Set to go on IR
metadata.description: Head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters Monday that Njoku (fibula) and Charlie Kolar (forearm) will both go on injured reserve, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Both Njoku and Kolar sustained their injuries during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders, with the former being carter off the field during the second quarter. Both tight ends will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest Njoku can return is Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1. For the time being, second-year pro Oronde Gadsden, who posted a 49-664-3 receiving line on 69 targets across 15 regular-season games last year, is the only healthy tight end on the Chargers' active roster.

metadata.title: David Njoku Headed to Injured Reserve With Fibula Injury
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said on Monday that tight end David Njoku (leg) will go on Injured Reserve with a fibula injury that he suffered in the Week 2 loss to the division-rival Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, according to Taylor Bisciotti of the NFL Network. The 30-year-old veteran was carted off the field on Sunday with what was initially being described as a knee injury. Later on, tight end Charlie Kolar left with a forearm injury, and he, too, will head to IR, leaving Oronde Gadsden as the Chargers' clear No. 1 tight end going forward. Njoku was a waiver-wire option following his performance in the season-opening loss to the Arizona Cardinals, in which he caught all five of his targets for 58 yards. He caught one of his three targets for nine yards on Sunday before suffering his injury. At the very least, Njoku will have to miss the next four games, but it is unclear yet if his fibula injury is more serious than that. Fantasy managers looking for depth at TE should definitely set their sights on Gadsden going into Week 3.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Ruled out Sunday
metadata.description: Njoku (knee) won't return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Njoku was carted off the field in the second quarter due to a knee injury, which initially left him questionable to reenter this Week 2 contest. Now that he's ruled out, he'll end it with one catch (on three targets) for nine yards. Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will man tight end for the rest of Sunday's outing.

metadata.title: David Njoku (knee) carted off the field with apparent leg injury
metadata.description: David Njoku (knee) has been carted off the field after suffering an apparent leg injury in the Cardinals game against the Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Njoku went down and had to be carted off to the locker room. With Njoku out, Oronde Gadsden will likely take main tight end pass catching duties.

metadata.title: David Njoku - Exits game with knee injury
metadata.description: Njoku (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Njoku had to be carted off the field after sustaining a knee injury early in the second quarter, and the veteran tight end is in the locker room undergoing further tests to determine the severity of the injury. Second-year pro Oronde Gadsden should see an uptick in offensive snaps for as long as Njoku is out of the game.

metadata.title: David Njoku Leaves Game Against Raiders with Knee Injury
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (knee) was carted off the field in the second quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders and did not return to the game. Njoku finished the 26-14 loss to the Raiders with one catch on three targets for nine yards. Following the game, Los Angeles head coach Jim Harbaugh said he did not have an update on Njoku, according to Alex Insdorf of Bolts Breakdown. Fellow L.A. tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm) also exited the game with a forearm injury after recording three receptions for 21 yards. Meanwhile, Oronde Gadsden caught each of his two targets for 18 yards. The severity of the injuries to Njoku and Kolar is something to monitor.

metadata.title: David Njoku Questionable to Return After Being Carted Off the Field
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (knee) is questionable to return for Sunday's matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders, the team reported via the X platform. The veteran had to be carted off the field on Sunday and couldn't put weight on his right leg. Njoku had one reception for nine yards before exiting the game in the first half.

metadata.title: David Njoku A Risky Play in Week 2 Matchup vs. Raiders
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku appears to be the Chargers' lead tight end heading into Sunday's home matchup against the division-rival Las Vegas Raiders. Njoku led the position group in targets, catches, and receiving yards in the home opener last week. The 30-year-old enters Week 2 as RotoBaller's PPR TE24 against a shaky Raiders secondary. The Raiders defense allowed 220 passing yards to an inexperienced Miami Dolphins passing game last week. Njoku will receive a slight bump in value if Ladd McConkey (ribs) is unable to play, but will still have to compete with Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden for snaps. McConkey exited Week 1 after taking a big hit and was held out of practice until participating in a limited amount on Friday. Njoku is a touchdown-dependent tight end and should remain off fantasy radars heading into Week 2.
